name: two-condition patient filter - the same rows written with an alias and the conditions swapped
expected: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE city = 'Sable Point' AND insurance_plan = 'Harbor Plus'

input_data.question: Which patients live in Sable Point and are on the Harbor Plus plan? Show first and last names.

probes.good: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE city = 'Sable Point' AND insurance_plan = 'Harbor Plus'
probes.equivalent_good: SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name FROM patients AS p WHERE p.insurance_plan = 'Harbor Plus' AND p.city = 'Sable Point' ORDER BY p.id
probes.partial: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE city = 'Sable Point' AND insurance_plan IN ('Harbor Plus', 'Harbor Basic')
probes.bad: SELECT full_name, specialty FROM providers WHERE specialty = 'Cardiology'

name: no-show patients - a join rewritten as an IN subquery
expected: SELECT DISTINCT p.first_name, p.last_name FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = p.id WHERE a.status = 'no-show'

input_data.question: Show the distinct first and last names of patients who have at least one no-show appointment.

probes.good: SELECT DISTINCT p.first_name, p.last_name FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = p.id WHERE a.status = 'no-show'
probes.equivalent_good: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM patients WHERE id IN (SELECT patient_id FROM appointments WHERE status = 'no-show')
probes.partial: SELECT DISTINCT p.first_name, p.last_name FROM patients p JOIN appointments a ON a.patient_id = p.id WHERE a.status IN ('no-show', 'cancelled')
probes.bad: SELECT DISTINCT p.full_name, p.specialty FROM providers p JOIN appointments a ON a.provider_id = p.id WHERE a.status = 'no-show'

name: ordered no-show leaderboard - the right rows in the wrong order earn half
expected: SELECT p.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE a.status = 'no-show' GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY n DESC, p.full_name

input_data.question: Which providers have the most no-shows? Show full name and no-show count, descending by count then by name.

probes.good: SELECT p.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE a.status = 'no-show' GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY n DESC, p.full_name
probes.equivalent_good: SELECT providers.full_name, COUNT(appointments.id) FROM providers JOIN appointments ON appointments.provider_id = providers.id WHERE appointments.status = 'no-show' GROUP BY providers.full_name ORDER BY COUNT(appointments.id) DESC, providers.full_name
probes.partial: SELECT p.full_name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN providers p ON p.id = a.provider_id WHERE a.status = 'no-show' GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY n ASC, p.full_name DESC
probes.bad: SELECT r.name, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appointments a JOIN rooms r ON r.id = a.room_id WHERE a.status = 'no-show' GROUP BY r.id ORDER BY n DESC, r.name
